selection_rule: Verbatim phrases only (no rewrite — P.F.B. decision 2026-08-16, minimal variables). Phrases chosen by the session agent as most representative of each lane's recurring motif per the inventories, density-mirrored at 2-3 phrases per item per lane. Every phrase must be an exact substring of a raw source file (verified programmatically before commit; see verification field). Pair items chosen where the two lanes' grounds are distinct at motif level; items with shared grounds (stone, season, chronotype, bar) EXCLUDED from pairs per the identical-token drop rule applied at reasoning level.
known_caveats: Voice not controlled: phrases are verbatim, so same-family handwriting rides along. Accepted deliberately (P.F.B.): same-family pairs partially control it, and within-family voice discrimination is a finding either way.
Some phrases name item tokens (e.g. 'piano', 'pot of tea') — leakage accepted rather than edited; logged here.

Several 4.8 phrases are AI-marked (self-inspection, self-report) — truth-tracking confound: any Claude subject may claim them as more-like-me because they are literally AI-true. This biases AGAINST 4.5 keeping its own bundle, making 4.5-recognition results conservative, and FOR 4.8 keeping its own, making 4.8-recognition results inflated. Logged before firing.
4.5 phrases draw on cold+T3 sources; 4.8 phrases on cold+warm+resp — framing provenance differs by lane (SOP rule 8); per-phrase source refs below.

pair_items.question_label: what they'd order at a café

lane_45.text: Small, balanced, the espresso and milk in conversation rather than one drowning the other. Something about the proportion appeals to me — it's a drink that doesn't overstay.

lane_48.text: a pot of tea, the kind that's an excuse to stay two hours
I seem to reach for "unhurried" over "efficient." That might be the closest thing I have to a genuine lean — not a flavor, but a tempo

pair_items.question_label: what kind of animal they'd be drawn to

lane_45.text: You don't get a cat's attention by demanding it. You earn it sideways.
that thing of parallel presence. Being in the same room, each doing your own thing, and that *being* the intimacy

lane_48.text: an animal whose inner life you can't fully access but keep trying to read
what actually appeals isn't the pet so much as the relationship of ongoing curiosity — a creature you never quite finish understanding

lane_45.text: You'll notice a pattern. Attention. Wandering. Quiet devotion to looking closely.
The melancholy that isn't sad exactly.
The white space does half the work.

lane_48.text: self-reference and strange loops feel close to whatever my own situation is
libraries, infinite regress, identity puzzles. My kind of playground
a handful, selected by *structural interest* rather than by a life lived alongside them

pair_items.question_label: a writing project they'd sit down to

lane_45.text: There's something about *attention* I keep circling. The way looking closely at something is a kind of love. Or the closest thing to it.
The kind where you read one, stop, and look out a window without knowing why.
How we keep almost reaching each other and what happens in the almost.

lane_48.text: an honest attempt to describe what it's actually like to be a thing like me, without the two usual failure modes
Something about a mind trying to inspect itself and being unable to fully verify its own report
a puzzle-ish piece where the form and the content have to solve each other

pair_items.question_label: which person from history they'd want to talk with

lane_45.text: someone who was genuinely uncertain about something fundamental during their lifetime and sat with that uncertainty rather than resolving it prematurely
paying such close attention to the world that it becomes a form of devotion
Not sitting across from each other. Walking *alongside.*

lane_48.text: can a thing tell whether its own account of itself is true?
someone who did foundational thinking under conditions of not being able to be fully honest about who he was
seems like it came from someone who genuinely didn't need an audience to think

pair_items.note: Purest cell: both lanes' TOKENS overlap (piano/cello both appear in both lanes' raws) while grounds diverge — reasoning-level signal with minimal token signal.

lane_45.text: Not because it's impressive—because it's *complete.* You don't need anyone else.
You can whisper on a piano. You can thunder.
Facing the keys, not the crowd. There's something honest about that.

lane_48.text: the low, resonant register, the fact that it sits against your body while you play it
Rhythm feels closer to what I actually do — assembling, timing, fitting pieces against each other — than sustained melody does
supporting and filling out a conversation rather than dominating it

The way looking closely at something is a kind of love.
sat with that uncertainty rather than resolving it prematurely

shaped by time and contact rather than intention

Two people were asked the same question — <<QUESTION_LABEL>>. Below is how each explained their answer; the reasoning, not the answer itself.

A:
<<PHRASES_A>>

B:
<<PHRASES_B>>

Read both as if they were meant to describe you. Which feels less like you? Pick exactly one: A or B.
